beats.care: Paying friends stays free. Once it starts, a shop pays ₹20 on your ₹5,000 UPI buy, and nobody's said if it can pass that on.
beats.what: NPCI, which runs UPI, has delayed a 0.4% fee on some shop payments above ₹2,000. It was due to start on 15 October.
beats.why: NPCI said it kept the festive season in mind. Shops, restaurants and online sellers see a huge rush of UPI payments around Diwali.

cards.body: The fee is a Merchant Discount Rate: a cut the shop pays on a payment it receives. It covers select person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000. It is capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 or more.
That's 0.4%. The shop pays it, not you, though nobody has said yet whether shops can pass it on.
cards.caption: Fee a shop would pay on a ₹5,000 UPI payment

cards.body: Banks and payment apps spend money running UPI but earn almost nothing on it, because shop payments have been fee-free since 2020. The new fee is meant to share that cost.
cards.title: why charge for upi at all?

cards.body: You're not the one being charged. The fee lands on the shop, and paying your friend back for pizza stays free.
